stories.headline: Wings' Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd talk relationship on pod
stories.summary: Azzi Fudd hosted Wings teammate Paige Bueckers on her podcast and the two discussed their relationship, Dallas' season and Fudd's recovery from knee surgery.
stories.body:
Dallas Wings teammates Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers, the past two WNBA No. 1 draft picks, spoke on Fudd's podcast Friday about a variety of topics, including a personal life update.

"We're not together anymore; it's been a while," Bueckers said on the "Fudd Around and Find Out" podcast. "[We] share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Bueckers and Fudd, who were teammates in college at UConn, said they felt the need to address their relationship status in part because of allegations it factored into the Wings picking Fudd at No. 1 in April. Fudd was chosen over TCU guard Olivia Miles, who went on to be the Rookie of the Year for the Minnesota Lynx. Spain's Awa Fam (Seattle Storm) was taken third, followed by teammates from the 2026 champion UCLA Bruins: Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics), Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) and Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo).

Fudd, Fam, Betts and Miles were all No. 1 at different points in ESPN's mock draft in the months before the April draft. Bueckers said her previous relationship with Fudd had no impact on Dallas' decision.

"We were not together before she got drafted," Bueckers said. "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points but was limited to just 30 games after an injury to her right knee led to season-ending arthroscopic surgery in August. She offered an update on her health.

"My offseason's been good," Fudd said. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy.

"I think there's a lot I can improve on. Especially the iso game; I feel like I'm not too comfortable with that yet. I know I'm capable of doing a little bit more. Watching someone like Paige who is able to create from anywhere ... that's great inspiration for me."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists, and was named to the All-WNBA second team as Dallas reached the playoffs as the No. 7 seed.

The Wings were eliminated in the first round by the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries. Bueckers said she learned a lot from her first playoff experience and complimented Golden State.

"The Valkyries' defense, I can't explain to you how tough they are," Bueckers said. "They swarm, they send bodies, they trap you, they blitz you, they're so connected. I'm glad I got to have that experience against them to open my eyes to what the playoffs are like -- the physicality, the pressure, the environment.

"And I'm proud of our season. I hated losing; I sat and was pissed about it for like a week. I reached out to [Sue Bird] about it, what was her first playoff experience like. I didn't play as well as I wanted to. But it was my first experience, going against a really good opponent, and I was learning and growing through it all."

Fudd and Bueckers also addressed the Wings' move to the 19,000-seat American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas next season after playing at UT Arlington's College Park Center, which seats over 7,000, since the franchise relocated to Texas in 2016.

"UTA was a vibe; we had a ball, we did our thing there," Bueckers said. "But definitely excited to move into Dallas. New times."

While the change in venue will lead to more eyes on Wings games, the two players said they're hoping for less scrutiny of any on-court behavior.

Both said fans shouldn't read into interactions the two have with each other or their teammates as anything other than normal team behavior. They also said they don't stand for "hate of any kind" or "tearing people down to lift us up."

"We've seen a lot of negativity," Bueckers said. "We've had stuff sent to us, stuff sent to our family, our friends. There's been some crazy things said about us. We still support each other, we're still going to be great friends, we're still going to be great teammates. All the negative things can be put aside, and you don't need to overanalyze everything."

Fudd added with a chuckle, "Also, we don't need messages [from fans] on what the other person's doing. We've addressed everything we need to, and the rest will stay with us."

stories.headline: Subtle reason Jillaroo will cause Cup final headaches
stories.summary: Jillaroos fullback Tamika Upton has explained why Jesse Southwell commanded selection for the World Cup final against New Zealand.
stories.body:
The numbers are impressive, but it's what doesn't show up on the stats sheet that Tamika Upton likes most about Jesse Southwell.

The Brisbane five-eighth won a tight selection battle to replace Sydney Roosters premiership winner Jocelyn Kelleher for Sunday's Women's World Cup final.

Kelleher started in three of Australia's four Cup games and was player of the match in the 40-0 win over Samoa on Test debut.

Southwell, who will partner Tarryn Aiken in the halves, filled her boots with 44 points of her own in the record-breaking 124-6 win over Wales.

Kelleher kicks goals too and shared a strong bond with Roosters teammate and halfback Aiken during their NRLW title win, but has been named in the 21 jersey for the clash with New Zealand.

"Tarryn and Jesse haven't played too much footy together, but I've been fortunate to play a lot with the both of them and watching them both link up is going to be pretty special," Australia and Brisbane fullback Upton said.

"The best thing about Jesse, and this goes unnoticed and without stats, is how much space she creates for the people outside of her.

"I've been fortunate enough to have that pretty much my whole career, and I'm excited for her to do that for Taryn and make her job a little bit easier.

"She's young, she's energetic, she's enthusiastic, she wants the ball and she wants to be a part of the game."

Australia cruised into the final four before receiving a welcome test in their comeback semi-final defeat of Fiji.

"The record-breaking games are probably not the best when you're prepping for finals footy, which is so different," Upton said.

"We've had the luxury of everything working out for us and that just doesn't happen when it comes to finals.

"So it was good to be under the pump."

stories.headline: Fantasy playbook: Week 10 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores
stories.summary: An all-encompassing look at the matchups to exploit or avoid and lineup locks in fantasy, as well as projected scores for all NFL games.
stories.body:
The Playbook is your one-stop shop for all your fantasy football decisions for Week 10, which kicks off Thursday night with a game between the Commanders and Giants.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for season-long leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start advice, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday after 1 p.m. ET.

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

WSH-NYG | NE-DET | KC-ATL | HOU-CLE | MIN-GB | JAX-TEN | MIA-IND

CAR-NO | BUF-NYJ | SEA-LV | LAR-ARI | SF-DAL | PIT-CIN | LAC-BAL

Washington Commanders @ New York Giants
Projected Score: Giants 26, Commanders 21

Lineup locks: Jayden Daniels, Malik Nabers, Isaiah Likely

Fantasy Scoop: Daniels was limited to a season-low 14.6 fantasy points against the Rams on Sunday. A floor around 14 points is pretty good, but the bad news is that he's been held in the 14-18 point range in four out of his six games and has cleared 21.0 points only once (Week 5 against these same Giants). Daniels has seven passing TDs and his rushing production has dipped in recent weeks. During his first three outings, he totaled a 21-203-2 rushing line. During his most recent three games, he's totaled merely a 10-49-0 line.

Daniels' career résumé suggests that he'll bounce back as a rusher, but this is a situation to monitor in a good Week 10 matchup against a Giants defense that allowed him a 9-103-2 rushing line and 32.3 fantasy points earlier this season. New York has surrendered the sixth-most QB fantasy points on the season.

Projected Game Total: 46.5 (8th highest)

Win Probability: Giants 66% (9th highest)

New England Patriots @ Detroit Lions
Projected Score: Patriots 28, Lions 27

Lineup locks: Drake Maye, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, DeMario Douglas, Sam LaPorta

Fantasy Scoop: Douglas was an afterthought in the New England offense last season, posting a 31-447-3 fantasy line on 44 targets across 17 regular-season games. A bigger part of the offense here in 2026, Douglas is already at 31-434-4 on 46 targets through nine games. "Pop" is fresh off a career-high 102 receiving yards on a season-high nine targets against Green Bay on Sunday. He has now produced 15-plus fantasy points in four of his last five games, having averaged 5.8 targets per game and scoring four TDs during the span.

With A.J. Brown in doubt for Week 10, Douglas is positioned for a big role against a Detroit defense that has, even after a good game against Miami last week, still allowed the third-most catches and seventh-most fantasy points to WRs. Douglas will remain in the WR2/3 mix as long as Brown remains sidelined, but is best sent back to benches once Maye's top target returns.

Shadow Alert: Williams vs. Christian Gonzalez

Projected Game Total: 54.9 (3rd highest)

Win Probability: Patriots 53% (12th highest)

Kansas City Chiefs @ Atlanta Falcons
Projected Score: Chiefs 28, Falcons 17

Lineup locks: Kenneth Walker III, Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce

Fantasy Scoop: Rice produced 9.9 fantasy points back in Week 1 and matched that season low against the Jets on Sunday. Those two duds bookended three games with 12-plus fantasy points -- his only other full games this season. Rice has delivered either one touchdown or 83-plus yards in four out of his five games, and while his usage is down from prior years, he has still handled six-plus targets in four consecutive full games (7.5 per game).

Rice isn't doing enough to warrant WR1 consideration. Still, even with Josh Downs added to the mix, he should remain locked into lineups this week against an Atlanta defense that has allowed the sixth-most catches and 13th-most fantasy points to receivers. Ja'Marr Chase (31.5) and Tee Higgins (20.2) both produced 20-plus points against the Falcons in Week 9.

Projected Game Total: 44.8 (10th highest)

Win Probability: Chiefs 84% (4th highest)

Houston Texans @ Cleveland Browns
Projected Score: Texans 25, Browns 21

Lineup locks: Nico Collins, Denzel Boston

Fantasy Scoop: C.J. Stroud put up 384 passing yards, five passing TDs and 35.4 fantasy points against the Chargers on Sunday. It was his best performance since Week 9 of his rookie season in 2023 (470 yards, 5 TDs, 41.8 points). Stroud has now delivered 20-plus fantasy points in four out of his past five games and has produced at least 16.5 points in seven of his eight games this season. The fourth-year QB hasn't done much with his legs (20-100-1), but his 16 passing TDs put him well on his way to a career high -- his prior best was 23 TDs in 2023 -- and he has thrown only two INTs.

Stroud is playing well enough that he's on the weekly streaming radar, though he has a tough assignment this week against a Browns defense that has allowed only three QBs to reach 14 fantasy points this season, including just one over its past five outings.

Projected Game Total: 46.1 (9th highest)

Win Probability: Texans 67% (8th highest)

Minnesota Vikings @ Green Bay Packers
Projected Score: Packers 23, Vikings 19

Lineup locks: Justin Jefferson, Matthew Golden, Christian Watson, T.J. Hockenson

Fantasy Scoop: With nine weeks in the books, Jordan Love easily leads the NFL in passing yards and sits third in passing TDs with 19. That's a big reason he has the third-most QB fantasy points -- and he has finished as QB7 or better in four of the past five weeks.

Despite the strong passing production, however, Love is not a recommended fantasy option in Week 10. The Minnesota defense has allowed the fewest completions, passing TDs (five) and QB fantasy points this season. Love did have some success against this defense in Week 1 (19.5 fantasy points), but in seven games since then, the Vikings have allowed a total of 47.7 QB fantasy points (6.8 per game). None cleared 12.9. Especially with Love offering very little with his legs (20-100-1), he's best left on benches in his toughest remaining matchup.

Projected Game Total: 42.3 (11th highest)

Win Probability: Packers 77% (5th highest)

Jacksonville Jaguars @ Tennessee Titans
Projected Score: Jaguars 32, Titans 15

Lineup locks: Trevor Lawrence, Bhayshul Tuten, Parker Washington, Carnell Tate, Jakobi Meyers

Fantasy Scoop: When we last saw the Titans (Week 8), Cam Ward enjoyed perhaps the best game of his young career. The 2025 No. 1 pick completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards (his first 300-yard game), with two TDs and no INTs. He added 41 yards on seven carries, which helped him post a career-high 26.3 fantasy points. Ward has now reached 20 fantasy points twice this season, although he has also fallen short of 12 points in five of his other six outings.

Ward, who totaled six all-purpose TDs over his first seven games, is a name to watch, but he can't be trusted as a fantasy option until he delivers big numbers on a consistent basis. He can remain on waivers this week against a good Jaguars defense that has allowed only eight passing TDs and the sixth-fewest QB fantasy points. Only two QBs (Joe Burrow, Stroud) have reached 15 fantasy points against Jacksonville this season.

Projected Game Total: 47.1 (6th highest)

Win Probability: Jaguars 96% (highest)

Miami Dolphins @ Indianapolis Colts
Projected Score: Colts 22, Dolphins 17

Lineup locks: Jonathan Taylor, Ollie Gordon II

Fantasy Scoop: Caleb Douglas' production has been all over the map this season. Following Sunday's 6-70-0 receiving line, the third-round rookie has reached 13 fantasy points in three games, with 70-plus yards in all three. On the other hand, he has fallen short of 8.5 fantasy points in his other two games, with fewer than 45 yards in both. During his five active weeks, Douglas has played on 79% of Miami's offensive snaps and has a solid 22% target share, but the inconsistent usage (six-plus targets in three games, but exactly three in the other two) makes him tough to count on in fantasy.

Douglas has emerged as perhaps the No. 1 target in Miami, but in an offense that sits near the basement in passing attempts and passing TDs (six), he's an unappealing flex -- especially this week with Kyle McCord under center and going against a Colts defense that has allowed the fifth-fewest WR catches.

Projected Game Total: 39.1 (13th highest)

Win Probability: Colts 63% (10th highest)

Carolina Panthers @ New Orleans Saints
Projected Score: Saints 25, Panthers 25

Lineup locks: Chuba Hubbard, Chris Olave, Tetairoa McMillan

Fantasy Scoop: Darren Waller exploded for an 8-90-1 receiving line on 10 targets against the Broncos on Sunday. Waller has been about as boom/bust as they come this season, having hit 18.0 fantasy points twice, but falling short of 7.0 points in four of his other six outings. In true "streaming TE" form, Waller has averaged only 4.7 PPG in the five games he didn't find the end zone.

Prior to Sunday, Waller had seen exactly two targets in three consecutive games and totaled 61 yards on two catches during that span. His playing time didn't change much Sunday and the increased workload can (at least somewhat) be traced to Pat Surtain II shadowing McMillan. Waller does have another good matchup this week (New Orleans has allowed the seventh-most TE fantasy points), but he remains what he has been all season: a TD-dependent wild card.

Projected Game Total: 50.2 (4th highest)

Win Probability: Saints 51% (lowest)

Buffalo Bills @ New York Jets
Projected Score: Bills 35, Jets 22

Lineup locks: Josh Allen, James Cook III, DJ Moore, Garrett Wilson

Fantasy Scoop: Breece Hall finally returned from injury on Sunday and the Jets' backfield usage was as follows: Hall handled 15 carries and four targets (eight routes) on 27 snaps, while Allen soaked up eight carries and two targets (15 routes) on 36 snaps.

While it's likely Hall was simply limited a bit in his first game back, Allen's strong play suggests this will remain more of a committee than it was earlier this season. That makes both backs tough to trust in fantasy against a Bills run defense that has been a bit better as of late, but also one that has allowed 10 TDs and the ninth-most RB fantasy points this season. Hall, who has 16-plus touches in all four games he has played this season, is the preferred flex option of the two.

Shadow Alert: Wilson vs. Christian Benford

Projected Game Total: 57.4 (highest)

Win Probability: Bills 90% (3rd highest)

Seattle Seahawks @ Las Vegas Raiders
Projected Score: Seahawks 28, Raiders 20

Lineup locks: Ashton Jeanty, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Brock Bowers

Fantasy Scoop: The Seahawks appear to have settled on a two-headed backfield committee featuring Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price. After playing only a limited role in his first game of the season (Week 8), Charbonnet jumped to a 56% snap rate. That allowed him to reach 77 yards on 16 carries, but only 9 yards on a pair of targets. Price, meanwhile, played on 38% of snaps, which translated to 24 yards on nine carries and 54 yards on four targets. Price's 11.8 fantasy points were easily his most in five appearances this season, but the receiving uptick (four targets in two straight games) is pointing in the right direction.

The timeshare will likely limit the upside of both backs, but the duo is set up with a terrific Week 10 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has allowed the most yards, the highest YPC (5.2) and the third-most fantasy points to RBs this season. Charbonnet should be in lineups as a solid RB2, while Price isn't far behind as a viable flex option in a good matchup.

Projected Game Total: 47.6 (5th highest)

Win Probability: Seahawks 72% (6th highest)

Los Angeles Rams @ Arizona Cardinals
Projected Score: Rams 29, Cardinals 11

Lineup locks: Kyren Williams, Trey McBride

Fantasy Scoop: Granted, it was against a tough Seattle defense, but Tyler Allgeier struggled to reach 46 yards on 17 carries Sunday and was held without a catch on two targets -- despite playing on 96% of Arizona's offensive snaps. It was disappointing, to be sure, after he totaled 191 yards and two scores against Dallas the week prior.

Allgeier's Week 10 outlook will depend on the status of Bam Knight, who missed most of Week 8 and all of Week 9 because of a concussion. With Allgeier and Knight sharing backfield duties during Weeks 6-7, Allgeier saw 26 carries and five targets on 74 snaps, compared to Knight's 22 carries and seven targets on 71 snaps. In that scenario, both backs would make for underwhelming flex options against a Rams defense that has allowed an NFL-low three TDs, 3.6 yards per carry (fourth lowest) and the sixth-fewest fantasy points to RBs.

Allgeier will be a more palatable flex option if Knight remains out, though you should note that he managed just 48 yards on 19 touches when these teams met back in Week 6.

Projected Game Total: 39.6 (12th highest)

Win Probability: Rams 96% (2nd highest)

San Francisco 49ers @ Dallas Cowboys
Projected Score: 49ers 29, Cowboys 26

Lineup locks: Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Javonte Williams, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Deebo Samuel Sr., George Kittle

Fantasy Scoop: Williams has been outstanding this season, but expectations will need to be lowered a bit this week against a 49ers defense that has been elite against the run. San Francisco is allowing 3.5 yards per carry (third lowest) and has surrendered a league-low two RB rushing scores this season. Williams has done most of his damage on the ground, ranking in the top 10 among backs in both carries and rushing yards, as well as second in rush TDs (nine) thanks to a league-high 18 carries inside the 5.

Williams actually paces the entire NFL in expected TDs (11.4). He also sits just inside the top 15 backs in both targets and receptions, which is notable, as the 49ers have surrendered the most RB catches this season. Although Williams' efficiency may not be as good as usual, his strong play and heavy usage -- especially near the goal line -- is enough to keep him in the fringe-RB1 mix.

Projected Game Total: 55.5 (2nd highest)

Win Probability: 49ers 60% (11th highest)

Pittsburgh Steelers @ Cincinnati Bengals
Projected Score: Bengals 24, Steelers 23

Lineup locks: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren, Chase Brown, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins

Fantasy Scoop: DK Metcalf has been busy this season, playing on a career-high 94% of offensive snaps and handling a 23.9% target share (his highest since 2022). But despite the consistent playing time, he hasn't been a reliable fantasy option. He has reached 16.5 fantasy points twice but has also been in the single digits five times. That includes two consecutive outings that featured receiving lines of 2-56-0 and 1-4-0 (only six targets in both).

Metcalf, who is scoring a career-low 9.7 fantasy PPG, is doing enough to hang in the WR3 mix, but he'll have his hands full this week against probable DJ Turner shadow coverage. Metcalf scored his lone touchdown of the season when these teams met back in Week 3, but with Turner aligning against him on his perimeter routes, he totaled just 31 yards on five targets in the game. Turner also shadowed Metcalf in both 2025 meetings between these teams, during which Metcalf was held to single-digit fantasy points (8.0, 9.9).

Projected Game Total: 46.7 (7th highest)

Win Probability: Bengals 53% (13th highest)

Los Angeles Chargers @ Baltimore Ravens
Projected Score: Ravens 22, Chargers 16

Lineup locks: Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers

Fantasy Scoop: The Chargers returned from their Week 7 bye with little to no changes to their fantasy nightmare of a backfield rotation. Against the Texans on Sunday, Omarion Hampton (13 carries, zero targets) and Kimani Vidal (seven carries, three targets) both played on 27 snaps, with Keaton Mitchell (seven carries and four targets) handling 17 snaps.

Hampton remains a minimal factor in the passing game (63 yards on 13 targets) and has been held to single-digit fantasy points in six of eight games, including four in a row. Vidal has yet to clear 10 touches in any game and has cleared 40 yards only once (56 in Week 5). Mitchell has been held to 11 or fewer touches in all but one game and, just like Hampton, has delivered four consecutive single-digit fantasy outings.

This backfield should continue to be avoided, especially against a Ravens defense that has allowed 3.6 yards per carry (sixth lowest) and 3.1 yards per target (lowest) to RBs this season.

Projected Game Total: 38.4 (lowest)

Win Probability: Ravens 70% (7th highest)

stories.headline: NBA trade deadline: Big questions for Knicks, Thunder and other top teams
stories.summary: With the NBA trade deadline looming, which title contenders should -- and could -- make a deal to improve?
stories.body:
With the start of the 2026-27 NBA regular season in the rearview, the Feb. 11 trade deadline is just over the horizon, and it's never too early to start discussing which teams need to keep their options open and potentially add talent over the next three months.

Injuries have plagued the league early on, with the Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves both losing major cornerstones of their roster for an extended period of time. Do these Western Conference contenders need to start filling out their rotations, or can they survive without their superstars until the postseason? And after a shaky start to the season, do the defending champions New York Knicks need to rethink their run back to the Finals with some roster moves?

As teams settle into the season, our NBA insiders break down what 10 playoff contenders lack, the constraints shaping their trade options and what's in store as the deadline approaches.

Order is based on the top 10 teams in ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI) as of Tuesday, Nov. 10.

Jump to a contender:

BOS | CLE | DET

HOU | LAL | MIN

NYK | OKC | PHI | SA

1. San Antonio Spurs (10-2)
Projected record: 62-20

Chances to make the conference finals: 58.5%

What they're missing: The Spurs are on a winning streak even without any games from Tobias Harris, their big offseason acquisition. It's hard to find a hole in one of the league's most complete, well-rounded rosters. Their depth, however, could use some improvement, so they won't be stuck playing deep from their bench with the likes of Jordan McLaughlin if one of their three guards goes down with an injury, as they did in the playoffs last year. -- Zach Kram

What they can pull off: The Spurs have the draft assets to swing a deal, but that does not mean general manager Brian Wright will look to be aggressive. With one of the best records last year, San Antonio elected to stand pat.

If the Spurs do look to make a move, they have an unprotected 2027 first-round pick from Atlanta and three additional tradeable first-rounders. They also have swap rights in 2028 (via Boston, if Nos. 2-30), 2030 (the most favorable of San Antonio, Dallas, Minnesota (if Nos. 2-30) and 2031 (via Sacramento). San Antonio has 12 tradeable second-rounders.

Keep an eye on whether San Antonio is willing to take back salary that stretches past 2026-27. With Victor Wembanyama's extension starting next season and sixth man Keldon Johnson a free agent, San Antonio is only $11 million below the luxury tax in 2027-28. -- Bobby Marks

What's next for San Antonio? San Antonio plans to play out the season with what's on the roster despite owning plenty of assets to make a move at the trade deadline. The Spurs appear to be somewhat thin at the center spot behind Luke Kornet, but the staff has been pleased with the progress made by rookie Tarris Reed Jr. in such a short time.

San Antonio understands that over the next two years, the roster could become expensive, with the club expected to sign Stephon Castle to an extension this summer, followed by an extension for Dylan Harper in the summer of 2028. Besides that, the Spurs are already experiencing somewhat of a numbers problem due to all the depth they've accumulated.

"There's not enough minutes to go around," coach Mitch Johnson said. "Unfortunately, I've got to play the bad guy and I'm not always going to be right. But I've got to make tough decisions in regards to only 240 minutes." -- Michael C. Wright

2. Oklahoma City Thunder (8-4)
Projected record: 58-24

Chances to make the conference finals: 43.5%

What they're missing: The Thunder are missing lots of rotation players, and their activity at this trade deadline will depend a great deal on when -- or whether -- they can project those injured players to return. Nique Clifford is another body on the perimeter, but he doesn't seem like a playoff difference-maker, so general manager Sam Presti might still be on the search for another defensively minded wing who can backfill some of the production of the injured Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Nov. 8 trade for Clifford does not eliminate Oklahoma City from making another trade. While the Thunder do not have a roster spot, they do have the $5.4 million expiring contract of Nikola Topic and the $4.9 million salary of a former first-round pick.

Because they are over the first apron, Oklahoma City cannot take back additional salary if either player is traded. The Thunder also have three trade exceptions ($5.8, $11.3, $17.7 million), seven tradeable first-round picks (including three in June) and 19 second-rounders. -- Marks

What's next for Oklahoma? Presti will be patient. The Thunder addressed the need for defensive-minded wing depth by making a buy-low trade for 2025 first-round pick Clifford, parting with a pair of second-round picks to acquire a player who has two seasons remaining on his rookie deal. Oklahoma City will explore the market for opportunities to upgrade over the next few months, but a big splash would be a big surprise.

It's not Presti's style, as the Thunder haven't made a major midseason trade since getting Kendrick Perkins in 2011. Yes, Presti has plenty of picks that could be used to put together a blockbuster deal. But he also has to prioritize future finances with the goal of keeping a contender-quality supporting cast around Shai Gilgeous-Alexander throughout his prime. -- Tim MacMahon

3. Boston Celtics (10-2)
Projected record: 59-23

Chances to make the conference finals: 57%

What they're missing: The Celtics rank only 22nd in defensive rebounding rate, which is an anomaly for a team coached by Joe Mazzulla. Boston has ranked 11th or better in this stat in every other year with Mazzulla at the helm, per Cleaning the Glass. This issue should be fixable based on Boston's roster, with the likes of Mitchell Robinson and Jayson Tatum -- an excellent rebounder for his position -- chipping in. If it continues, Boston might be in the market for another big body who can help grab rebounds in the playoffs. -- Kram

What they can pull off: Last season, the Celtics were one of the league's more active teams ahead of the trade deadline. The four separate trades dropped Boston below the luxury tax while also creating a $27.7 million trade exception. The exception is available until February, but the first apron hard cap prevents Boston from using more than $10 million of it.

This year, the Celtics do not have to trim payroll but do need to keep an eye on the luxury tax, which they are currently $1.75 million below. Boston's most valuable asset could be its open roste spot. Because they are below the first apron, the Celtics will be able to sign a waived player with a preexisting salary of $15 million or more -- Marks

What's next for Boston? Finding another big man could be high on the Celtics' list. One thing the Celtics have learned from the Knicks is not overtaxing Mitchell Robinson, who plays well in spurts, and keeping him around the 20-minute mark is ideal. Keeping Tatum and Paul George fresh would be paramount as well, especially with Tatum still working his way back to his new normal in his first full season following an Achilles injury in 2025. The $27 million trade exception could go a long way, especially if they view the Eastern Conference as winnable. -- Vincent Goodwill

4. Houston Rockets (9-3)
Projected record: 55-27

Chances to make the conference finals: 23.8%

What they're missing: Only two Rockets perimeter players are shooting better than 37% on 3-pointers this season, and one of them is Bogdan Bogdanovic, whose injury track record suggests it might not be safe to count on him over the full season. Kevin Durant and Reed Sheppard should improve as the season continues, but it might behoove Houston to grab one more shooter in the meantime. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Rockets have two appealing trade assets in this upcoming draft: the right to swap with Brooklyn and an unprotected first-round pick (via the Phoenix Suns). Houston has four additional first-round picks available to trade, a $13.3 million trade exception and an open roster spot. The Rockets are allowed to use the full exception and still exceed the first apron. -- Marks

What's next for Houston? Despite owning plenty of assets and a trade exception, it's likely Houston will continue -- like last season -- to refrain from making any moves. Especially now that its roster has been revamped with the offseason additions of Bogdanovic and Marcus Smart, along with the return of point guard Fred VanVleet. The overall size throughout the roster gives the Rockets plenty of flexibility to utilize multiple lineups and combinations of players without sacrificing production and performance. VanVleet's absence last season somewhat sped up the development of Sheppard, Amen Thompson, Tari Eason and Jabari Smith Jr.

Still, Houston could probably use some depth at the center position, given the injury concerns regarding Steven Adams (right calf strain) and Clint Capela (right ankle sprain), who are both expected to return to the lineup soon. But unless the Rockets encounter a deal they can't refuse at the deadline, it's likely they stand pat. -- Wright

5. New York Knicks (6-5)
Projected record: 54-28

Chances to make the conference finals: 42%

What they're missing: The Knicks had, by definition, a championship-level roster last season, and the only player they lost was Robinson. Andre Drummond has served as a serviceable replacement so far, and it's difficult to imagine New York finding many better options on the trade market. But if one presents itself, then that's the clearest spot on New York's roster worth improving. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Knicks faced the same limitations last season but were still able to trade for backup guard Jose Alvarado. This season, New York is $809,000 below the second apron and is not allowed to sign a player until Feb. 14. The Knicks can use Pacome Dadiet's $3 million expiring contract in a trade but cannot take back more salary. New York is not allowed to sign a player waived who had a preexisting salary of $15 million or more. The Knicks have one first-round pick and 12 second-rounders available to trade. -- Marks

What's next for New York? The Knicks are putting off contract issues until the offseason and there's not a lot of flexibility, especially with owner James Dolan proclaiming he won't go into the second apron. If Mikal Bridges continues to struggle, do the Knicks start to canvas the league? But then again, he's owed over $116.5 million over the next three seasons, including a player option in 2029-30. The hope is that he turns it around similar to last season, because this team is in need of shot creation and shotmaking. -- Goodwill

6. Los Angeles Lakers (11-2)
Projected record: 54-28

Chances to make the conference finals: 13.9%

What they're missing: The Lakers have the best offense in the league but rank in the bottom half on the other end of the floor, and specifically they're 28th in defensive rebounding rate, ahead of only the Bulls and Suns. Kevon Looney is not the answer at backup center behind Walker Kessler, and although Sandro Mamukelashvili is a decent option, it's safe to add the Lakers to the long list of teams that could use another competent bruiser on their bench. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Lakers depleted their draft assets in the Kessler sign-and-trade which left them with the right to swap their 2028 first-rounder as their most significant remaining draft asset. The Lakers have three tradeable second-rounders (from 2031 to 2033, with two belonging to the Washington Wizards).

From a roster standpoint, Los Angeles could look to package the contracts of Jaden Hardy ($6 million) and Jarred Vanderbilt ($12.4 million) for a player earning $26 million or below. Despite being hard-capped at the first apron, the Lakers are $8.1 million under and are allowed to take back additional salary. Los Angeles has 15 guaranteed contracts and would need to waive or trade a player to open a roster spot. -- Marks

What's next for Los Angeles? After looking into trade packages to clear up a roster spot during the preseason, the Lakers ultimately had to waive former first-round pick Dalton Knecht in order to cut down to the maximum 15-player allotment. Coach JJ Redick has pretty much stuck to a 10-man rotation so far, with Vanderbilt overtaking Looney in the depth chart when Mamukelashvili isn't in as the stretch 5.

Redick still has to see what he has in second-year forward Adou Thiero and rookie Cameron Carr, although neither figures to be the solution to L.A. ranking second-to-last in the league in rebounding. Still, as one Eastern Conference executive told ESPN, "so long as Doncic, [Austin] Reaves and Kessler stay healthy, the Lakers will be fine." Reaves is now dealing with a left heel injury that forced him to exit the team's win over the Bucks on Wednesday night. -- Dave McMenamin

7. Minnesota Timberwolves (8-3)
Projected record: 54-28

Chances to make the conference finals: 26%

What they're missing: Entering the season, it seemed as if the Timberwolves' big issue was going to be frontcourt depth after they traded Julius Randle and Naz Reid in the offseason. But second-year Frenchman Joan Beringer has done an excellent job backing up his countryman, Rudy Gobert, and Trey Lyles, after a season out of the NBA, has performed surprisingly well at the backup power forward spot. Does Minnesota trust that that will continue, though, or would the team rather pursue a sure thing at the position? -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Timberwolves were one of the big winners last February when they acquired Ayo Dosunmu. Because of that trade and the offseason addition of LaMelo Ball, Minnesota's draft assets are limited. They have no first-round picks available to trade and one second-rounder (2030 via Memphis; if Nos. 51-60).

One player to watch could be Cody Williams, who is on an expiring $6 million contract after Minnesota declined his team option for next season. Apron rules prevent Minnesota from taking back more salary than they send out, so the return of Donte DiVincenzo, who tore his Achilles during the 2026 playoffs, could be the Timberwolves' big addition at the deadline. -- Marks

What's next for Minnesota? Keep biding time until Anthony Edwards' return. Minnesota should be thrilled with how it has played since its franchise guard underwent knee surgery after playing just four games to start the season. The Timberwolves are 5-2 without Edwards and boast the NBA's top-ranked defense. The schedule will get tougher, but they have held up well in the face of a potentially season-altering injury.

Ball continues to assimilate well to his new surroundings after an offseason trade, and fellow newcomer Jonathan Kuminga has made a good first impression after so-so stops with the Warriors and Hawks. Meanwhile, Dosunmu has been excellent as Edwards' stand-in replacement.

With Edwards projected to return as soon as late December or early January, Minnesota should have plenty of time to evaluate its full roster before the Feb. 11 trade deadline. -- Ben Golliver

8. Detroit Pistons (7-3)
Projected record: 55-27

Chances to make the conference finals: 44.4%

What they're missing: The Pistons' greatest need is the same as it has been for the last 18 months: a second scorer and playmaker next to Cade Cunningham. Duncan Robinson is the only other perimeter player averaging more than 12 points per game. And although Daniss Jenkins has done an admirable job as a backup, he's not a championship-level No. 2 option. Luckily, the Pistons have plenty of trade assets they could use in a deal for a fellow star. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The Pistons are among a handful of teams that control each of their next seven first-round picks. They can trade up to four and can swap in each season. Detroit also has 11 seconds available. And, despite $90 million committed to Cunningham and Jalen Duren this season, Detroit is $14.5 million under the first apron hard cap.

However, putting together a trade package without including a starter or key rotation piece could be difficult. To match salary, the Pistons have only the sizable contracts of John Collins ($17 million), Robinson ($16 million) and Isaiah Joe ($11.3 million). None have guaranteed salary obligations past this season.

For Detroit to use its $5.2 million or $15 million trade exception, it would need to open a roster spot. -- Marks

What's next for Detroit? The Pistons once again look poised to be among the top teams in the East during the regular season, even without making a move at the deadline. A year ago at the deadline, with a young team playing better than expected, Detroit chose not to rock the boat. This front office has chosen patience in letting its core of young players grow so far, so it's worth watching if an opportunity presents itself for a bigger swing and how the Pistons handle it this time around. -- Jamal Collier

9. Philadelphia 76ers (9-3)
Projected record: 49-33

Chances to make the conference finals: 21.1%

What they're missing: The 76ers don't have proper championship-level depth at center behind Joel Embiid, who is the single greatest injury risk for any team in the championship picture. Lineups with LeBron James at center can function on occasion, but that's not a permanent solution, and with Ariel Hukporti out for the season after tearing his Achilles, Philadelphia needs a better backup big man ahead of Jabari Walker and Adem Bona. -- Kram

What they can pull off: The 76ers have an open roster spot and Hukporti's $3.4 million expiring contract. Because they are $1.8 million under the first apron hard cap, they are allowed to take back up to $5.2 million of salary. They also have 10 second-round picks available to use in a trade. Philadelphia can sign a player with its open roster spot starting on Dec. 4. -- Marks

What's next for Philadelphia? Coach Nick Nurse said that big man Dominick Barlow, who has missed all of this season with a back injury, is expected to be cleared for on-court activities by mid-November. The Sixers are thin in the frontcourt, with Bona missing time with a neck injury, Hukporti out for the season and Tacko Fall missing time with a quad injury.

For now, the Sixers have been excited by how Walker has played as the team's backup center. Walker, too, missed time with a knee injury but has proven to be the team's most consistent backup center option this season. He had his best game this season in a win over the Bulls, finishing with nine points and 11 rebounds.

"He probably deserves to play more, to be honest," Nurse said this season. -- Kris Rhim

10. Cleveland Cavaliers (6-6)
Projected record: 47-35

Chances to make the conference finals: 11.8%

What they're missing: Cleveland ranks 29th in the league in defensive turnover rate, per Cleaning the Glass, ahead of only the woeful Milwaukee defense. This is still a decent defensive unit overall, thanks to the efforts of Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen near the rim. But Cleveland's backcourt looks tremendously exploitable in the playoffs; even reserves Sam Merrill and rookie Meleek Thomas are more offensively minded. The Cavaliers are in desperate need of another perimeter stopper. -- Kram

What they can pull off: Five players (Mobley, Allen, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson and James Harden) combine to earn 85% of the cap this season, making a trade difficult unless they are willing to part ways with Allen, or reserves Merrill and Jaylon Tyson. The Cavaliers are $45,000 below the first apron this season and have no tradeable first-round picks and only one second-rounder available. Cleveland can fill their open roster spot starting on April 9. -- Marks

What's next for Cleveland? After Harden took the place of Darius Garland at last season's deadline, the Cavs brought back their core four, believing that continuity will make a difference this season. But Cleveland is currently leaning on some younger players, such as Tyson, Thomas and Tyrese Proctor to fill out its depth off the bench. Keep an eye out for whether that trio can continue to produce or if the Cavs will look for moves similar to last season's deadline when they added veterans such as Dennis Schroder and Keon Ellis in an attempt to fortify their depth. -- Collier

stories.headline: Brewers' Misiorowski, Yanks' Schlittler crowned unanimous Cy Young winners
stories.summary: Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski and New York's Cam Schlittler capped dominant 2026 seasons by sweeping all 30 first-place votes to win their respective Cy Young Awards.
stories.body:
Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler, the two most dominant starters in baseball in 2026, were named unanimous Cy Young Award winners Wednesday.

Misiorowski, the ace of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, received all 30 first-place votes for the National League honor in his first full big league season, finishing ahead of Cristopher Sanchez of the Philadelphia Phillies in second and Chris Sale of the Atlanta Braves in third.

Schlittler, the New York Yankees' breakout No. 1 starter, swept the American League award also in his first full major league campaign, with Dylan Cease of the Toronto Blue Jays in second place and Parker Messick of the Cleveland Guardians in third.

San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Toronto Blue Jays closer Louis Varland won the Baseball Writers' Association of America's inaugural Reliever of the Year award in their respective leagues.

Varland earned 16 of the 30 first-place votes for the AL honor. The right-hander's 1.27 ERA across 78 innings was the lowest in the majors among qualified relievers. He finished the season with 35 saves in 71 appearances.

Miller took the NL award unanimously after logging one of the best reliever seasons in recent history. The right-hander was an overwhelming force late in games, logging a 1.67 ERA with 38 saves and 129 strikeouts -- the most in baseball among relievers -- in 70 innings across 66 appearances. He finished with a 47.6% strikeout rate, sixth all time among pitchers with at least 50 innings pitched.

Miller's 101.4 mph average fastball velocity was tops in the majors. Misiorowski, incredibly, wasn't far off.

Misiorowski, 24, went 16-5 with a 1.80 ERA, 0.80 WHIP and 252 strikeouts in 30 starts across 174⅔ innings -- leading the majors in ERA, WHIP, and strikeouts -- as the Brewers won an MLB-best 103 games. His 6.6 fWAR led all pitchers. His 232 ERA+ was the best for a full season since Pedro Martinez recorded a 291 ERA+ in 2000.

He became the fourth Cy Young Award winner in Brewers franchise history, joining Corbin Burnes (2021), Pete Vuckovich (1982), and Rollie Fingers (1981). He is the first pitcher since Randy Johnson in 2001 to win the Cy Young and World Series in the same season. He is the third pitcher since 2000 to win both the Cy Young Award and World Series in the same season.

"I'm going to go hunting next week with my dad," Misiorowski said. "And that quiet time in the stand is really going to be my opportunity to think about this year. And think about all the positives that we had, and what to work on and what I need to do, to do this again next year."

The historic performance was fueled by unprecedented velocity. Misiorowski's fastball averaged 100.6 mph, unparalleled territory for a full-time starting pitcher. He threw more than 1,000 pitches at 100 mph or faster -- more than double the record Jordan Hicks set in 2018. He threw more pitches at 101 mph or faster than every other pitcher combined from 2008 through 2026. His fastest pitch, a 105.5 mph heater in June against Pete Crow-Armstrong, was the fastest pitch ever thrown by a starting pitcher in the Statcast era.

The 6-foot-7 Misiorowski took the league by storm as a rookie in 2025, controversially making the NL All-Star team as a replacement after only five starts. But he struggled down the stretch with a 5.36 ERA over his final 10 outings before compiling a 1.50 ERA in 12 innings across three relief appearances in the postseason. This year, he harnessed the heat.

This year, he harnessed the heat. Misiorowski carried a 3.31 ERA over his first six starts through April before establishing himself as the best pitcher in the sport with a 1.46 ERA in 142 innings over his final 24 starts. The stretch included a one-hit shutout with 15 strikeouts and no walks against the Phillies on June 12. He finished the season with 10 double-digit strikeout outings before posting a 1.89 ERA in 19 innings across four playoff starts, including the Brewers' World Series-clinching Game 5 win less than a year-and-a-half after making his major league debut.

"It's happened really quick," Misiorowski said. "It's crazy, the opportunity that I got in front of me and being able to take a hold of that and run with it is really cool. It's been a crazy two years, year and a half or whatever it is. It's been fun."

Schlittler, 25, became the seventh Yankee -- and the first since Gerrit Cole in 2023 -- to win the award. Of the seven, only he, Ron Guidry, and Whitey Ford were homegrown.

He didn't throw quite as hard as his NL counterpart, but his three-fastball mix confounded hitters all season. He complemented a four-seam fastball that routinely touched triple digits and averaged 98 mph with a 94.6 mph cutter, 97.8 mph sinker, and power curveball he incorporated more later in the season.

The Massachusetts native -- and Boston Red Sox fan growing up -- finished 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA and 239 strikeouts in 193⅔ innings over 33 starts for a pitching staff that posted the best ERA in the majors. He gave up one run or fewer in 21 starts. He was at his best away from Yankee Stadium, logging a 1.16 ERA in 17 road starts. He led the AL in ERA, fWAR (6.2), and ERA+ (215). Only Spud Chandler (1.64 in 1943) and Guidry (1.74 in 1978) have posted a lower ERA as qualified starters in franchise history.

He plowed through lineups with an uncommon confidence and fire, becoming invaluable for a Yankees rotation that dealt with extended absences from Cole, Max Fried, and Carlos Rodon.

"Realistically, I look at it and I'm just happy," Schlittler said. "The goal, honestly, coming into the season was to stay healthy, be consistent, and make all my starts. That's something I was able to do."

A seventh-round pick out of Northeastern in 2022, Schlittler flew under the radar as he rose through the minor leagues because his stuff did not scream dominance. His fastball velocity averaged in the low 90s in his first full professional season in 2023. But with a few delivery tweaks and added muscle, the velocity gradually climbed until he reached 100 mph for the first time in his major league debut at Yankee Stadium in July 2025.

He found his footing in his fourth start three weeks later and was a revelation down the stretch and into the postseason. In Game 3 of the AL Wild Card Series, he held the Red Sox scoreless over eight innings with 12 strikeouts and no walks, which solidified his standing among the game's best pitchers.

The Yankees entered 2026 with Schlittler firmly in their rotation. They hoped for continued growth from a resounding rookie campaign. He exceeded all expectations with one of the greatest pitching seasons in the franchise's history. He's already shooting for more.

"I definitely could have had a better season," Schlittler said. "Obviously, I had a few hiccups along the road. Realistically, I think there's things I can get better at and that's not going to be specifically in one area of the game. But just being out there on the mound and making certain adjustments in the game. Again, I feel like this season was great, but as you look at how I finished, things could have definitely been better."

Also Wednesday, Miller was a unanimous winner of the Trevor Hoffman NL Reliever of the Year Award, and the Rays' Bryan Baker was named the Mariano Rivera AL Reliever of the Year. The Hoffman and Rivera honors are voted on by a panel of former relievers and are separate from the BBWAA awards, which are voted on by BBWAA members.

Other MLB awards handed out Wednesday:

Comeback Player of the Year: Yordan Alvarez, Houston Astros (AL); Zack Wheeler, Philadelphia Phillies (NL)
Edgar Martinez award (outstanding DH): Yordan Alvarez
Hank Aaron award (top offense performer): Yordan Alvarez (AL); Pete Crow-Armstrong, Chicago Cubs (NL)
Executive of the Year: Erik Neander, Rays

stories.headline: Wysh List: Will Connor McDavid break 200 points? The cases for and against
stories.summary: The Oilers superstar is on pace to break a benchmark that hasn't been hit since the 1980s.
stories.body:
Connor McDavid is going to score 200 points this season.

I truly, truly believe this.

Or at least I want to believe it.

It has happened only four times in NHL history, all by players named "Wayne Gretzky." The Great One's apex was 215 points in 1985-86, a single-season record that McDavid's early points-per-game pace (2.53) is threatening. That's also the last time any player hit 200 points in the NHL.

The 200-point season was a forgotten relic of the 1980s, like acid wash jeans or Spuds MacKenzie. It made sense that Gretzky or Mario Lemieux could push for 200 points in an era that didn't have structured defensive systems, goalies with refined technique or, like, Russians.

McDavid's scoring pace so far is frankly unfathomable. I never thought I'd see a player break 200 again without some fundamental change to the NHL, like making regulation 3-on-3 or altering the dimensions of the net itself to soccer goal widths.

The mind boggles that someone might legitimately threaten to hit 200. But then McDavid has a way of boggling the mind.

"It seems so unrealistic, that number 200, but you look at what he's done so far ... if there's anyone that's going to do it, it's him," Devils forward Luke Evangelista told me recently. "He's putting up video game numbers right now. Like it's on 'easy mode.' I literally can't believe the start that he's had."

McDavid scored 48 points in his first 19 games this season, including 11 goals. Entering Wednesday night's game against the Philadelphia Flyers, McDavid was on pace to tally 212 points, which would tie Gretzky's 1981-82 total for the second most in league history. He was also on pace for 163 assists, which ESPN Research said would tie Gretzky's 1985-86 total.

McDavid is the fourth player in NHL history with 48 or more points before his 20th game, and the fourth player to have a 19-game point streak to start the season. He has three five-point games and two four-point games.

Hitting 200 points, a mark no one has legitimately threatened to hit in nearly 40 years, is in his sights.

So how is he doing this?

When asked about his personal achievements, McDavid has consistently deferred to his Oilers teammates. I know he recently said that he's not a robot, but the constant deflection of praise over the course of his career very much feels like a programmed prime directive.

"I'm playing with some special players. That helps. Getting some bounces, too," he said recently. "When the team is winning games, I've been the beneficiary of some great team play."

McDavid has also credited his start to the Oilers having made a coaching change, one that my colleague Mark Messier infamously noted was rubber-stamped by McDavid himself. Mike Babcock has the Oilers playing a more structured defensive scheme, and McDavid said that has reinvigorated him.

"It's actually been really fun to just dive in and have to sink your teeth into a new system, a new way of playing. It's left my own [game] secondary. Just trying to take care of the things I need to do within the system," he said. "It's just been a byproduct of everybody playing well."

Defenseman Mattias Ekholm said the Oilers are aware of, but not discussing, McDavid's push for 200 points.

"Can he do it? Absolutely. Is it a thing that we go around here or that he thinks about? Not really at all. We're just trying to do our best every game. I know he is as well. That's what makes him special," he said. "He just wants the team to win, wants the team to have success. And when the team does have success, it's usually because he's playing great. So it's awesome to see."

Ekholm acknowledged that he didn't think McDavid had another level to his game, and has his own theory as to why McDavid has been able to reach it. The veteran defenseman told me that last season's playoff flameout -- losing in the first round to the Anaheim Ducks -- might have ironically been the best thing for McDavid.

Obviously, the early ouster meant more recovery time than McDavid has had in the previous four postseasons -- and when you factor in 4 Nations Face-Off and the Olympics, that's a lot of hockey.

"I'm 100% certain it's the rest. The fact that we got knocked out early in the playoffs, you get another two months to get the body rested up," Ekholm said. "Those two long runs, they'll take a toll on the body."

But Ekholm also told me something interesting about losing early vs. having your dreams crushed in the Stanley Cup Final, as McDavid and the Oilers experienced in 2024 and 2025.

"When you're knocked out in the first round and you get punched in the nose a little bit, I think that can help with your mental space and your motivation," he said.

"You reevaluate yourself in a bigger way when you lose in the first round than you maybe do in the finals, because you're so close and you're almost trying to find excuses as to why you didn't go all the way. There are no excuses for losing in the first round. So it's just different."

So Connor McDavid is rested physically and mentally, and somehow hungrier after getting dispatched by the Ducks than he was when the Florida Panthers batted him away from the Stanley Cup. And he has decided to take this out on the record books.

But the most likely reason for this historic offensive start is also the most obvious one:

He's Connor Flippin' McDavid, a hockey deity with an unparalleled combination of speed, agility, vision, reflexes and on-ice IQ.

"It's easy to get intimidated by a guy like that. If he's able to turn and burn, he's going to make you look bad," Devils forward Connor Brown said.

Brown has been McDavid's friend since their days with the OHL's Erie Otters and were teammates for two seasons in Edmonton. He has texted McDavid during this bonkers start to the season. Brown has long thought 200 points was in McDavid's reach.

"I remember going to Edmonton a few years ago and I thought that was always in the cards," he said.

I think he does it. I think he breaks 200.

Sadly, that puts me in direct contrast with people much smarter than I am, ones who know math and stuff.

"I'll take the side of 'no' for the following math reasons," said Vince Masi, a research producer at ESPN.

Here's a sampling of what a Council of Big Brains said when I asked them if McDavid will hit 200 points:

Vince Masi, ESPN
McDavid has averaged 75 games played in a season over the previous three seasons. If he were to maintain his current pace of 2.53 points per game and play 75 games, he would be on pace for 189 points.

He'll have to play in 80 games while maintaining the current pace just to get the pace to 200-plus and would be a pace for 202. Over the past three seasons, the highest points-per-game rate in a month was 1.90 in December, so he'd have to overperform even higher than his already high pace.

A more realistic goal is to break his own mark for points in the salary cap era when he had 153 in 2022-23 -- and he played in all 82 games that season. There's bound to be some sort of regression, and not necessarily directly from him.

The Oilers are shooting 26.7% on the power play when he's on the ice, which would be four percentage points better than his single-season career high of 22.5% in 2022-23. They're shooting 16.9% at 5-on-5 with him out there, which would be five percentage points better than his previous high in 2019-20 and 2020-21.

For perspective, the NHL leaders this season in 5-on-5 shooting percentage are the Avalanche and Capitals (as of Nov. 10) at 12.6%. Stathletes projects McDavid for 166 points based on his shot quality and passing quality.

Rachel Doerrie, ESPN
No, he will not get 200. But, barring injury, I think he hits 170, which would be the first time in the modern era since Lemieux.

There are dog days of the season, teams tighten up defensively and they'll try to adjust to him. I also believe he'll focus more defensively in March to prepare for the playoffs, and might even get some rest as well. He's slowing down (only two points per game now) and I think 170 is probably the ceiling here, which should have him 30 points ahead of the next player -- and a unanimous MVP winner.

Jack Fraser, HockeyStats.com
McDavid has done the near impossible so far this season, there is absolutely no doubt about that. But doing that over 19 games is very different than doing it in 84.

So far this season, No. 97 is clicking at a 16.9% on-ice shooting percentage at 5-on-5 and 5.25 on-ice goals per 60 minutes. His norm, even with his own skill and the skill of his frequent linemate Leon Draisaitl is 10.4% and 3.7. Right now, the Oilers are scoring 1.9 goals above expected every 60 minutes with him out there. To even approach any of these numbers in a full season would be beyond unprecedented.

You might say "Hey! This is McDavid we're talking about here!"

[I sheepishly raise my hand]

But we've already seen the regression begin -- in the past 12 games, he has been at roughly league average marks and has six 5-on-5 points. It just so happens that the power play got super hot. That's all before you get into considerations like ice time, how long the Oilers will keep him and Draisaitl together, etc.

In short, we will probably forget about the race to 200 by February, if not quite a bit earlier, once he has gone through his version of a cold streak or if Babcock finally changes things. I would put the smart money somewhere between 160-170 if he stays healthy and plays all season with Draisaitl. That's still one of the best seasons in NHL history, certainly the best since Lemieux.

Mike Kelly, NHL Network
I'm going to break my rule, which is never bet against the superstars, but I don't think 200 is likely.

McDavid would need to score at a 2.34 points-per-game pace the rest of the way. He's higher than that through 19 games, but his career high in a full season is 1.87. It's remarkable what he's doing and I hope he does it, but I will say unlikely.

OK, so the analytics community isn't in "The 200 Club" with me and Connor. The conventional thinking is that he taps out at around 170 points, which would be the highest total since 1988 and the first time anyone not named Gretzky or Lemieux even broke 160 points.

But here's the takeaway: If he gets to 170 points or higher, McDavid will have orchestrated perhaps the single greatest individual offensive season in NHL history.

As I referenced earlier, players like Gretzky, Lemieux and Bobby Orr were rewriting the record book in eras that never approached the quality of talent, speed, depth and defensive obstacles that McDavid faces today. In the 1980s, there were 24 instances of players scoring at least 135 points, with 10 different players hitting that mark. Since the 2005-06 NHL reset, it has happened four times: Twice by McDavid, and once by Nikita Kucherov (144) and Nathan MacKinnon (140).

When Alex Ovechkin was chasing Gretzky's goals record, a popular theme was that even if he fell short it would have been an all-time accomplishment given the era in which he plays. I'm not saying that McDavid's projected 170 points should be rounded up to a "modern gentleman's 200"; just that hitting 170 in 2026-27 should stand next to Gretzky's elephantine 215 points when one considers the era.

But I still think he breaks 200, even if it defies the math and he logic. It's Connor. It's what he does.

"Every time you think that he's found another level, he finds another level," Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, McDavid's teammate in Edmonton since he entered the league, told me. "We're not putting it past him, that's for sure. There's no doubt in our minds that he can just keep climbing, keep breaking records and keep hitting numbers that we haven't seen in a long time."
